item.title: Swedish pro-government parties 'agreed on a plan' for second term in power
item.description: Sweden's four pro-government parties have "agreed on a plan" for their second term in power at a cosy meeting at the Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's house, which also involved Christmas presents and tasteless festive jumpers.

item.title: UN slams Sweden's 'discriminatory' push to tighten citizenship rules
item.description: A UN committee has sharply criticised immigration reforms pushed through by Sweden's government, arguing that plans to tighten citizenship requirements were "discriminatory", while stop-and-search zones were "illegal".

item.title: Swedish word of the day: wallenbergare
item.description: Today’s word is a Swedish dish thought to be based on the Swedish equivalent to the Rockefellers.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Nobel prize banquet set for this evening, woman detained for hospital poisonings, UN slams Swedish citizenship laws as 'discriminatory' and other news from Sweden on Wednesday.

item.title: 'I hate to be stereotypical but the light in northern Sweden is amazing'
item.description: In this week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra, we hear from the Umeå-based Canadian writer. Mandy Pipher about what it's been like moving to Umeå in northern Sweden.

item.title: How will the finances of people in Sweden improve in 2026?
item.description: The coming year promises to be a good one financially for people living in Sweden, with the economy emerging from a long slump, real wages improving, and the government showering the population with tax cuts.

item.title: How to decorate your Christmas tree like a Swede
item.description: So you're celebrating a Swedish Christmas, but how do you make sure that your tree meets expectations?

item.title: Planned night train service between Switzerland and Sweden scrapped
item.description: In October, Swiss national railways (SBB) announced the launch, in April 2026, of a night train connecting Basel with the Swedish city of Malmö, and had even started to sell tickets for this route. This move, however, was premature.

item.title: Sweden bucks global trend as income gap narrows
item.description: Sweden has become slightly more equal over the past decade, with the income gap between the top 10 percent and the bottom 50 percent of earners dropping marginally, according to the World Inequality Report by the French economist Thomas Piketty.

item.title: How to survive and maybe even enjoy Sweden's long, dark winters
item.description: The winter solstice is approaching (this year it's on December 21st) and in Sweden that means darkness. It can be a hard time of year ‒ I've heard it described as “four months of depression” ‒ but there are ways to make it easier, and even to enjoy it.
